q: Do fine bubble diffusers cut ETP aeration electricity?
title: Fine bubble aeration in an ETP
short: Usually yes. Aeration blowers are often the largest electricity user in an effluent plant. Fine bubble diffusers transfer more oxygen per kWh than coarse bubble systems or surface aerators. Add dissolved oxygen control so blowers slow down when demand drops, and compare blower kWh per kL treated before and after.
audience: Textile, food, pharma and chemical units with ETPs

ul: Effluent treated per day in kL.
Dissolved oxygen readings, to show treatment did not suffer.

p: Poor aeration can create anaerobic zones that release methane. Good aeration control helps both energy and methane.

senseible: Senseible reads fuel invoices and electricity bills and applies IPCC 2006 factors and the CEA grid factor (0.710 kg CO2 per kWh), so you can compare Scope 1 and 2 before and after a change from the documents themselves.

sources.label: 2006 IPCC Guidelines for National Greenhouse Gas Inventories
